structure:
A 78-line Markdown ruling, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md, by Sam on 9 October 2026 about templates and the dashboard. It opens with three verbatim quotes (answers-2026-10-09-pm.md points 8, 8a and 7b) and a short framing paragraph saying the ruling only covers what splitting off the templates theme needs, and that claims marked 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle' are the orchestrator's calls, not Sam's words. Then 7 numbered claims in two sections: (a) The dashboard, claims 1 to 3 (INS dashboard summary information blocked; the rest of the INS home goes ahead; the animals notification list stays in the animals frontend, with a new theme restyling it and plants reframed alongside); (b) Templates, claims 4 to 7 (templates CRUD goes ahead with 4 listed areas; template mode walks the same pages without forking; template rows drop look-or-order dependencies on other themes, with the transporter-list note; plants takes the same change in the same increment, with 4 bullets). Scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. It cites plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json and ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 22 as context, but those are separate sources and not part of this one.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, The whole ruling: Part 1 read the whole 78-line ruling file, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md, top to bottom. Lines 3-26 hold three verbatim quotes from Sam (answers-2026-10-09-pm.md point 8 on the INS front door, point 8a on what 'the dashboard' means and on templates, point 7b on plants). Lines 28-30 are the orchestrator's framing paragraph: the templates theme is split off for a second machine, the ruling covers only what that needs, and claims marked 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle' are not Sam's own words. Section (a) The dashboard holds listed claims 1-3; section (b) Templates holds listed claims 4-7, with the bullets under 4, 6 and 7. Each listed claim was checked against the three quotes: what the quotes say in so many words is verbatim, what only the listed claim (or an orchestrator's application) says is inferred with the reason, and what the ruling touches but leaves open is a gap. Covered: all three quotes, the framing paragraph, claims 1 to 7 and every sub-bullet, plus gaps on dashboard timing, the INS notification lists, template-mode validation, discard versus delete, and how firm the animals dashboard restyle is.

claims.statement: The templates theme is split off from the rest of the design release 2.1 backlog and built on a second machine while the rest of the backlog is still being ruled on.
claims.quote: Sam wants the templates theme split off and built on a second machine while the rest of the backlog is still being ruled on. This ruling covers only what that needs.
claims.note: Written by the orchestrator as framing; it reports Sam's wish rather than quoting him.

claims.statement: Claims in this ruling marked 'applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle' are the orchestrator's calls, not Sam's own rulings, and carry less weight than his words.
claims.quote: Claims marked "applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle" are the orchestrator's calls, not Sam's own words.
claims.note: Applies to claim 3's plants sentence, claim 6's transporter-list paragraph and all of claim 7. The 'carry less weight' half is read from sources.json's role for this source.

claims.statement: When Sam blocks 'the dashboard', he means only the dashboard's summary information (how many notifications, how many status changes), not other controls on the INS home page.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template. Do I need to be that explicit? The dashboard, as in the summary information that you have this many notifications or this many status changes.

claims.statement: The INS dashboard's summary information showing the count of notifications is blocked: no changes are made to it in this programme.
claims.quote: That stuff's blocked. We can't be making changes. ... The dashboard, as in the summary information that you have this many notifications or this many status changes.
claims.note: New (claim 1 says New).

claims.statement: The INS dashboard's status-change cards (how many status changes) are blocked.
claims.quote: The dashboard, as in the summary information that you have this many notifications or this many status changes. That's all massive stuff.
claims.note: 'cards' is claim 1's word, not Sam's.

claims.statement: The drill-downs from the INS dashboard's summary information are blocked.
claims.quote: INS front door: overall dashboard, drill-downs and the notification lists. Here, the dashboard stuff is really early. The INS dashboard requirements are still really early days. That stuff's blocked.

claims.statement: The dashboard summary information is blocked because its requirements are at a very early stage and have not been checked with anyone; it stays blocked until those requirements firm up.
claims.quote: The INS dashboard requirements are still really early days. ... That's all massive stuff. Has not been sort of bounced off anyone.

claims.statement: Backlog rows for the dashboard summary information stay in the backlog, marked blocked, rather than being removed; the area is re-distilled once its requirements exist.
claims.quote: Those rows stay in the backlog, blocked, and the area is re-distilled once requirements exist.
claims.note: Inferred: the listed claim says it; Sam's quotes say only that the dashboard is blocked, not how its rows are handled.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say when the INS dashboard requirements will firm up, who will agree them, or what triggers the re-distil of the blocked area.

Point 8 names 'the notification lists' as part of the INS front door alongside the dashboard and drill-downs before saying 'That stuff's blocked', but the ruling does not say whether an INS-level (cross-journey) notification list is blocked; claim 3 only settles the animals list.
claims.note: Ambiguity recorded, not resolved.

claims.statement: Nothing else on the INS home page is blocked by the dashboard block: only the summary information is.
claims.quote: I block the dashboard, as in the fucking dashboardy bit. Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: New (claim 2).

claims.statement: The 'Use template' button on the INS home page goes ahead.
claims.quote: Not a button on there to create a template.
claims.note: Inferred: Sam exempts 'a button on there to create a template'; the button's label 'Use template' is claim 2's.

claims.statement: The 'Create new' button on the INS home page goes ahead.
claims.quote: Its "Create new" and "Use template" buttons, the "What are you importing?" question before a notification is created, and the Templates navigation item go ahead.
claims.note: Inferred: Sam's quotes do not name a 'Create new' button; it follows from his limiting the block to the summary information.

claims.statement: The 'What are you importing?' question, asked before a notification is created, goes ahead.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md claim 2, lines 38-39; claim 4 fourth bullet
claims.quote: the "What are you importing?" question before a notification is created
claims.note: Inferred: listed in claims 2 and 4 but not named in Sam's quotes; follows from the block covering only the summary information.

claims.statement: The Templates navigation item goes ahead.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-09-templates.md claim 2, line 39; claim 4 third bullet
claims.quote: the Templates navigation item go ahead
claims.note: Inferred: listed in claims 2 and 4, not named in Sam's quotes; follows from templates being CRUD that goes ahead.

claims.statement: A backlog row that depends on the INS home page depends only on the 'Create new' and 'Use template' buttons, the type question and the Templates navigation item existing, not on the dashboard summary information.
claims.quote: A row that depends on the home page depends only on those controls existing, not on the summary information.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam limiting the block to the summary information; the dependency rule is the listed claim's wording.

claims.statement: The live animals notification list stays in the animals frontend and is not moved to the INS frontend in this programme.
claims.quote: Something we could potentially do, maybe as a separate theme, is changes to the animals dashboard, so the animals dashboard looks more like the animals dashboard on the prototype.
claims.note: Inferred: Sam blocks the INS front door's lists and suggests changing the animals dashboard instead, which implies the list stays where it is. Claim 3 says New.

claims.statement: A new, separate theme changes the animals frontend's own dashboard so it looks like the animals dashboard on the prototype.
claims.quote: Something we could potentially do, maybe as a separate theme, is changes to the animals dashboard, so the animals dashboard looks more like the animals dashboard on the prototype. That'd be good.
claims.note: Sam hedges ('potentially', 'maybe'); claim 3 states it firmly as a new theme.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say which parts of the prototype's animals dashboard the animals frontend restyle must match, nor whether Sam's 'potentially, maybe' makes the theme optional.
Plants' own notification list is reframed in the same increments as the animals dashboard restyle.
claims.quote: Applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle (point 7b): plants' own notification list is reframed in the same increments (`plants-common-mapping`, point 7c).
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle ('[Plants] and animals get that change at the same time'), not Sam's words. Evidence cited: plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json, point 7c.

claims.statement: For this programme, the move of the animals notification list to the INS frontend, which claim 22 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 kept from design release 1, no longer applies.
claims.quote: Replaces, for this programme, the move of the list to the INS frontend that claim 22 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 kept from DR1.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam's point 8 suggestion to change the animals dashboard in place. Supersedes claim 22 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 for this programme only.

claims.statement: Templates are simple create, read, update and delete work and go ahead now.
claims.quote: "Create a template" is fucking crud. That's simple.
claims.note: New (claim 4).

claims.statement: A Manage templates area goes ahead as part of the templates work.
claims.quote: Manage templates
claims.note: Inferred: listed under claim 4; Sam's quote calls templates CRUD but does not name Manage templates.

claims.statement: A user can start a template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'Create a template is crud' (create).

claims.statement: A user can save a template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'crud' (create/update).

claims.statement: A user can view a template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'crud' (read).

claims.statement: A user can change a saved template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'crud' (update).

claims.statement: A user can use a template to start a notification.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred: the listed claim and the 'Use template' button of claim 2; 'to start a notification' is read from that button sitting beside 'Create new'.

claims.statement: A user can discard a template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'crud'.

claims.statement: A user can delete a template.
claims.quote: starting, saving, viewing, changing, using, discarding and deleting a template
claims.note: Inferred from 'crud' (delete).

claims.statement: The ruling lists discarding and deleting a template separately but does not say how they differ (for example, discarding an unsaved template in progress versus deleting a saved one).
Template mode is another way of walking through the same journey pages, not a separate set of pages.
claims.quote: Mate, this needs to be another way of walking through the same pages, maybe capturing the same data with different validation.
claims.note: New (claim 5).

claims.statement: Template mode captures the same data as the notification journey.
claims.quote: maybe capturing the same data with different validation
claims.note: Sam hedges with 'maybe'.

claims.statement: Template mode may apply different validation from the notification journey on the same pages.
claims.quote: maybe capturing the same data with different validation. I don't know

claims.statement: The ruling does not say which validation differs in template mode: whether fields mandatory for a notification are optional in a template, whether any validation is skipped, or what is checked on saving a template.
claims.note: Sam says 'I don't know' on this point.

claims.statement: Template mode is built so later changes to the journey pages carry into template mode without rework.
claims.quote: Guess what? There are going to be changes again in the future. You can't be fucking implementing something in such a way that it can't handle journey changes.

claims.statement: Template mode must not copy journey pages for templates.
claims.quote: It must not copy pages or fork the journey for templates.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam's 'another way of walking through the same pages'.

claims.statement: Template mode must not fork the journey for templates.
claims.quote: It must not copy pages or fork the journey for templates.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam's 'another way of walking through the same pages' and his demand that it handle journey changes.

claims.statement: Template rows do not wait for other themes' changes to the pages they walk through; they work on the pages as they stand when built, and later page changes carry over.
claims.quote: you can't fucking go, "Right, we're just going to finish development forever, and then we'll take a coffee."
claims.note: Inferred: Sam rejects waiting for the journey to be finished before building template mode. Claim 6 has no 'New' marker of its own on line 60 but the claim ends 'New.' after the transporter paragraph.

claims.statement: A template row keeps a dependency on another theme's row only where it needs something that row creates and that does not exist today, such as a page, a field or a stored value.
claims.quote: A template row keeps a dependency on another theme's row only where it needs something that row creates and that doesn't exist today, such as a page, a field or a stored value.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam's point 8a principle that template mode must not wait for the journey to stop changing.

claims.statement: A template row's dependency that exists only because a page's look or order will change is dropped; examples are the overview's new regions, the review's new headings and the reordered opening run.
claims.quote: A dependency that exists only because a page's look or order will change is dropped. Examples are the overview's new regions, the review's new headings, and the reordered opening run.
claims.note: Inferred from Sam's point 8a principle. The three examples name other themes' rows (overview regions, review headings, opening-run order) that template rows must not depend on.

claims.statement: In template mode, the transporter list's buttons follow today's transporter list.
claims.quote: Applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle: the transporter list's buttons in template mode follow today's transporter list.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 8a principle, not Sam's words.

claims.statement: Transporter management is blocked separately, and template rows do not wait on it.
claims.quote: Transporter management is blocked separately (answers point 5).
claims.note: Answers point 5 of answers-2026-10-09-pm.md; the block itself comes from another ruling. 'template rows do not wait on it' is read from the preceding sentence's 'follow today's transporter list'. The orchestrator's call.

claims.statement: Where a change applies to common pages or behaviour, plants and animals get that change at the same time, rather than in separate increments.
claims.quote: A workflow: go through and identify common pages, common behaviour, and where it's required. [Plants] and animals get that change at the same time.

claims.statement: Increments are not split to check for or add a plants equivalent, because adding an increment is relatively expensive and doubling the increments is overkill.
claims.quote: it's massive overkill to double the number of increments to see if there's an [plants] equivalent. ... The overhead of adding an increment is relatively expensive, so we don't want to be needlessly separating things.

claims.statement: Where a templates row changes something plants also has, the same increment changes plants.
claims.quote: Applied by the orchestrator from Sam's principle (point 7b): where a templates row changes something plants also has, the same increment changes plants.
claims.note: The orchestrator's application of Sam's point 7b to templates, not Sam's words. Evidence cited: plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json.

claims.statement: Starting from the INS 'What are you importing?' type question gives plants the same entry as animals: choosing plants creates a plants draft notification and lands on plants' first page.
claims.quote: Starting from the INS type question: gives plants the same entry, creating a plants draft and landing on plants' first page.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle.

claims.statement: The Templates navigation item is added to plants' navigation too, linking across to Manage templates.
claims.quote: The Templates navigation item: added to plants' navigation too, linking across to Manage templates.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle. 'linking across' implies Manage templates lives outside the plants frontend.

claims.statement: Back links follow the context a page was opened in, in plants as in animals.
claims.quote: Back links: follow the context a page was opened in, in plants as in animals, using plants' own step order.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle.

claims.statement: Plants' context-following back links use plants' own step order, not animals'.
claims.quote: using plants' own step order
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle.

claims.statement: Only animals has a Back link from its first page to the INS type question; plants does not, because plants' first page is its own type question.
claims.quote: Animals only: Back from the first page to the type question, because plants' first page is its own type question.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call from Sam's point 7b principle ('where it's required').

claims.statement: Template mode is animals only: it is not added to plants pages, because templates cover the animals sets.
claims.quote: Template mode on plants pages is also animals only, because templates cover the animals sets.
claims.note: The orchestrator's call. The wording 'Template mode on plants pages is also animals only' is awkward; read as: plants pages get no template mode. 'the animals sets' is not defined in this ruling.
